newsitem.title: USA: Sallie Mae disappointed with advisory firm report.
newsitem.headline: Sallie Mae disappointed with advisory firm report.

text.p: Student Loan Marketing Association Tuesday said it was disappointed with the decision of Institutional Shareholder Services, an institutional shareholder advisory firm, to support the call by a shareholder group for a special meeting of Sallie Mae shareholders.
Sallie Mae said the decision "to support the call of Albert Lord for a special meeting of shareholders gave insufficient weight to corporate governance changes made by Sallie Mae last week."

Lord is the spokesman for the Committee to Restore Value at Sallie Mae and a Sallie Mae director. The committee had asked shareholders to call a special meeting to vote on a plan of reorganization and to choose the reorganized company's board of directors.
Sallie Mae said Lord's special meeting would be separate from the special meeting called by Sallie Mae for May 15 to consider and vote on the company's plan of reorganization.

Sallie Mae last week said it made significant changes to the corporate governance structure of its proposed plan. Once adopted, Sallie Mae said, the new governance structure will allow shareholders broad authority to make changes to the board. This removes any rationale for another special meeting, Sallie Mae said.
Sallie Mae said the ISS report has not yet taken any position on the plan of privatization to be considered at Sallie Mae's special meeting.
Sallie Mae said it made the statement in response to inquiries.
